messages:
Sam: Kicking off handoff for NovaHealth POC. Customer wants private VPC deployment. Must keep client source IP visible to their backend and have a single static outbound IP for allowlisting. Also want a short list of firewall ports and rough pricing delta between Dedicated vs Private for budgeting.

Nora: Two high-level patterns we usually propose: (A) PrivateLink endpoint in their VPC + customer-owned NAT for leaving the VPC (keeps egress IP on their side); (B) cross-account VPC peering + our managed egress/proxy that uses our reserved EIPs. Tradeoffs: PrivateLink = easier, less routing work, no CIDR collisions; Peering = lower latency for some flows but requires route table upkeep and CIDR coordination.

Ben: For the "preserve client source IP" requirement, simplest is to let their NatGateway/EIP be the internet-exit point. If they absolutely need our single IP, we can offer a managed egress proxy that we pin to a customer EIP pool, but note: scaling events can cause IP rotation unless we reserve EIPs and route through a static NAT instance/proxy. That setup needs a network ticket & security signoff.

Sam: Can you give me the minimal port list to send to their infra team? They run strict egress policies.

Ben: Minimal whitelist we ask customers to open:
- Outbound TCP 443 to our service (or to the pinned EIP if using our egress)
- DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to their resolver if using PrivateLink and internal name resolution
- ICMP optional for troubleshooting
(We do not require other custom ports for TLS API calls.)

Nora: Example SG snippet for creating the interface endpoint: 
```
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-123 --service-name com.redwood.inference --vpc-endpoint-type Interface --subnet-ids subnet-abc subnet-def --security-group-ids sg-allow-redwood
```
And SG rules: inbound TCP 443 from their app subnets, outbound ephemeral allowed.

Sam: Pricing note for sales deck: what do I quote for a 30-day POC? They asked if we can do Dedicated trial pricing for Private deploy.

Nora: POC approach we recommend: offer a 30-day Dedicated trial (reserved capacity credits) to validate throughput/latency, while we set up Private deployment in parallel. Dedicated trial reduces unit cost for evaluation. Private deployment pricing includes an integration/setup fee + per-node runtime. I'll DM you ballpark numbers for the deck.

Ben: Security checklist items raised by their SOC: mTLS, audit logs, and VPC flow logs. We support mTLS for service-to-service and can turn on detailed auth/audit events in the control plane. For PrivateLink, they still control flow logs on their VPC/subnets.

security-bot: Note: Customer questionnaire Q12 - "Does Redwood preserve original client IPs in our logs?" Answer: If the customer routes egress via their own NAT, yes; if they use Redwood-managed egress proxy, we can include X-Forwarded-For and log the original IP, but customer firewall logs will see the proxy IP.

ops-bot: Created ticket POC-NOVA-118: "NovaHealth private deploy network setup & egress IP decision" assigned to Ben.

Sam: Action items: (1) Ben to confirm whether our infra team can reserve EIPs for a single-customer proxy (ETA 4 business hours). (2) Nora to share Dedicated trial credit approval language for the quote. (3) I'll schedule a 20-min network walk with customer and ask them to have a network engineer on the call.

Ben: I'll post the candidate EIP ranges and the short allowlist once I hear from infra. Expect a short note in ~3hrs.

Nora: I'll also add a mini runbook comparing PrivateLink vs Peering with pros/cons for NovaHealth's SOC to review.

Sam: Thanks all 44d
